title: Spotted Owlet — ISO 10,000
subtitle: Two Spotted Owlets at the Bandhavgarh tiger reserve, shot at ISO 10,000 on an OM-1 micro four-thirds sensor. Fine feather detail and dark plumage stress noise reduction and sharpening simultaneously.

images.title: RAW
images.caption: Original RAW with no editing, shot at ISO 10,000.

critique.text: As the original unprocessed RAW file shot at ISO 10,000, this image serves as the baseline. It exhibits heavy luminance and chrominance noise across the entire frame, which significantly obscures fine details in the owls' feathers and the tree bark. While the underlying focus appears accurate, the sharpness is completely masked by the noise. High-level overview of edits: All software successfully eliminated the base noise, but the differences lie in detail rendering. DxO (Image 1) and Lightroom (Image 7) excelled at preserving natural, fine details. Topaz provided good results depending on the sharpening applied, ranging from slightly soft (Image 5) to natural (Image 4) to slightly over-done (Image 3). ON1 (Image 2) struggled, replacing noise with unnatural painterly artifacts. Overall ranking of edits: 1st: DxO (Image 1), 2nd: Lightroom (Image 7), 3rd: Topaz Default (Image 4), 4th: Topaz Wildlife (Image 3), 5th: Topaz NR Only (Image 5), 6th: ON1 (Image 2).

images.title: Lightroom Denoise
images.caption: Lightroom's new AI Denoise with default setting of 50

critique.text: Lightroom's AI Denoise has performed exceptionally well here relative to the noisy RAW. The noise is completely eradicated, leaving a very clean and smooth background. What makes this edit stand out is the natural preservation of detail in the feathers and bark without any harsh sharpening artifacts. It competes very closely with the DxO edit; while the DxO might have a tiny bit more micro-contrast pop, this Lightroom version looks incredibly organic and true-to-life. A top-tier result.

This image demonstrates exceptional noise reduction while maintaining and enhancing fine details. The DeepPRIME XD3 processing has successfully eliminated the heavy high-ISO noise present in the original RAW file without introducing significant artifacts. The sharpness is outstanding, particularly noticeable in the fine feather details around the owls' eyes and the texture of the tree bark. It looks very natural, avoiding the over-processed look seen in some other edits. This is one of the strongest results in the set.

images.title: Topaz Photo 2
images.caption: Topaz Photo with default noise reduction only (strength 69, original detail 0) plus default sharpening across whole image

critique.text: This version uses default sharpening along with noise reduction and yields a very solid result. The background noise is gone, and the sharpness is much improved over the RAW file. Compared to the Wildlife sharpening setting in Image 3, this feels more balanced and natural, avoiding harsh edges. However, it still falls slightly short of the DxO processing in terms of extracting the absolute finest natural-looking details from the feathers.

images.title: Topaz Photo 3
images.caption: Topaz Photo with default noise reduction only (strength 69, original detail 0) plus sharpening with Wildlife setting across whole image

critique.text: This edit provides excellent noise reduction, effectively cleaning up the high-ISO grain of the original RAW. The application of the Wildlife sharpening setting has definitely increased perceived sharpness and brought out detail hidden in the noise. However, compared to the DxO edit or even the default Topaz sharpening in Image 4, it feels slightly over-sharpened. The edges of the feathers are a bit harsh, creating a slightly crunchy micro-contrast that looks less natural than the top performers.

images.title: Topaz Photo
images.caption: Topaz Photo with default noise reduction only (strength 53, original detail 0)

critique.text: This image shows the result of applying noise reduction without additional sharpening. It is remarkably cleaner than the original RAW, with the heavy ISO 10,000 grain mostly removed. Because no extra sharpening was applied, it is noticeably softer than the other Topaz edited versions (Images 3 and 4). While it looks very natural and avoids any over-processing artifacts, it lacks the pop and fine detail definition that makes the DxO or Lightroom versions stand out.

images.title: ON1 RAW
images.caption: Processed in ON1 RAW using NoNoise and TackSharp combined

critique.text: While the NoNoise feature has successfully removed the base noise from the original RAW, the combined TackSharp processing has resulted in a heavily over-processed image. The details, especially the owls' feathers, look unnatural, smeared, and almost painterly or plasticky. It lacks the fine, crisp resolution of individual feather structures seen in the DxO or Lightroom edits, trading noise for bizarre artifacts. This is the weakest edit in the set.
